summary.headline: United Foodbrands Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 40.9% YoY to INR429 crores on 24.5% same-store sales growth, with growth volume-led.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR429 crores, up 40.9% YoY, with same-store sales growth of 24.5% and dine-in transaction volumes up about 56%. Pre-Ind AS restaurant operating margin was 13.4% (up about 520 bps YoY) and pre-Ind AS adjusted operating margin was 6.1% (up about 500 bps). Margin was held back by higher corporate overhead (10.3% of revenue vs 6.5% in Q1), incremental loyalty provisions (about 0.3% of sales), pre-opening hiring, and inflation. Management kept the 300-restaurant target by end FY27 but did not reaffirm FY27 margin guidance numerically, deferring to H2 improvement.

segments.name: Barbeque Nation India
segments.commentary: Same-store sales growth 27.8%, revenue growth 41.4%, dine-in transaction volume growth 60.8%; about 85% of business from dine-in. Average revenue per outlet INR6.4 crores in H1 FY27, with mature stores at about INR7 crores.

segments.name: Barbeque Nation International
segments.commentary: Same-store sales growth 26.5%, revenue growth 59%, dine-in transaction volume growth 64%, despite regional geopolitical backdrop. Launched digital and value-led marketing in Middle East and session-wise pricing analytics; entered Thailand this quarter with high initial setup costs.

segments.name: Premium CDR (Toscano, Salt)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth 28.5%, same-store sales growth 7.8% (base 5.5%), dine-in volume growth about 25%. Estate grew from 23 to about 42 restaurants over two years; South India mature margins above 18%, while Mumbai and Delhi newer restaurants are still building base and the company paused new openings there for two quarters.

guidance_outlook: Cross 300 restaurants by end FY27; 19 restaurants under construction to open in Q3 and Q4 (about 9-10 per quarter).
Medium-term plan to add 40-50 restaurants annually, funded mainly from internal accruals; internal target of about 500 restaurants by FY30, with public FY30 guidance raised to 425-450 from about 400.
Long-term SSSG expectation of 5-7%; management declined to guide next-year SSSG.
Some H2 margin benefits expected; management said it is not chasing a specific margin number on a specific date, and inflation is running above prior expectations.
Employee cost inflation guided at about 6-7% for back-end staff and 2-3% for store staff.
Margin levers cited: gross margin recovery, mature-portfolio ROM expansion, new-cohort maturation, and corporate overhead leverage.
capex_capacity: 9 restaurants opened in Q2 FY27 (5 in Q1); network stood at 274 restaurants at quarter end.
19 restaurants under construction for Q3 and Q4 FY27 openings.
Expansion funded primarily from internal accruals; net debt marginally higher in the quarter as capex was largely offset by operating cash flow.
Rightsized new store format at about 3,000 sq ft, reducing rent, utilities and fixed overhead per store.
Big Buffet format (average price about INR450) runs in about 25% of restaurants, mainly in Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets.
demand_pricing: No price hike taken in the last four quarters; average realisation down about 7-8% YoY in Q2, partly from Big Buffet mix.

Management said demand is broad-based: every market grew in double digits and all four regions posted SSSG above 20% in Q2; North India (about 40% of business incl. UP and Bihar) was affected by Navratri timing.
Over 80% of dine-in customers now pre-reserve, versus about 70% a year ago; about 90% of dine-in volume comes via captive channels (app, website, call centre, walk-ins).
Loyalty programme adoption up about 3x YoY; delivery grew about 47-50% YoY across Barbeque in a Box, UBQ and Dum Safar.
Management described itself as the largest player in its segment, with the second player about one-fifth to one-sixth its size. Competition cited as 5-star and 4-star buffets priced 30-50% higher.

qa_highlights.question: How will average revenue per Barbeque India store move from INR6.4 crores toward the INR9-10 crore potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited throughput optimisation in weekday and weekend lunches, deeper captive engagement, delivery value SKUs, and selective future price increases once volumes stabilise. Some restaurants already exceed INR9 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin is flat at about 55.5% against guidance of 100-150 bps improvement; why?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said realisation is down about 7-8% YoY with no price hike in four quarters, plus mix shift to Big Buffet. Gross margin is up month-on-month from Q4 to Q2 and procurement scale benefits are offsetting inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Corporate cost rose to 10.3% of revenue from 6.5% in Q1; how much is pre-opening cost versus permanent overhead?
qa_highlights.answer: Hiring in back-end culinary, digital, tech, marketing and regional operations was largely complete; full-quarter effect is now in Q2. Loyalty provisions added about 0.3% of sales. Management did not give a specific FY27 margin number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the October 2026 SSSG on a two-year basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give the figure, citing Navratri moving from September last year to October this year, and said average revenue per restaurant continues the H1 momentum.

qa_highlights.question: Why only about 40-50 openings a year when site economics and cost per store have improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is building capability in business development, site, project, legal and operations teams. It is open to moving higher and cited internal target of about 500 restaurants by FY30.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise Q1 to Q2, and is it a run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no one-offs; hiring for new stores 15-45 days before launch and full-quarter effect of Q1 openings drove costs. Back-end inflation 6-7%, store staff inflation 2-3%.

risks_watch: Corporate cost ratio (10.3% of revenue in Q2) and whether it falls as revenue scales.
Gross margin recovery against inflation and no price hikes in four quarters.
Premium CDR SSSG in single digits and the recovery of Mumbai and Delhi newer restaurants.
Conversion of Q3 and Q4 openings (19 under construction) and whether the 300-restaurant target is met by FY27 end.
SSSG comparison base from Q4 FY27 onward; management declined to guide next-year SSSG.
International expansion (Thailand launch, high setup costs) and regional geopolitical risk.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, volumes and unit economics, with strong statements on the brand and new-store cohort. More cautious and evasive on margin timing and SSSG guidance: no numeric FY27 margin reaffirmation, no October two-year SSSG figure, and no next-year SSSG guidance.
key_quotes: We are now in our fourth consecutive quarter of strong broad-based performance, and the business trajectory is looking very strong.
Our growth continues to be entirely volume-led.
I'm not chasing a number on a specific date, but as these levers unlock, this will help.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Pre-Ind AS restaurant margin 13.4% (up about 520 bps YoY) and mature portfolio at 14.7%, but corporate cost jumped to 10.3% of revenue from 6.5% in Q1, gross margin is flat at about 55.5-65.5% (conflicting figures), and no numeric FY27 margin guidance was reaffirmed.

rows.why: 19 restaurants under construction for Q3 and Q4 openings (about 9-10 per quarter) on a 274-unit base, about 7% of network per quarter, taking the network past 300 by FY27 end; 9 opened in Q2 after 5 in Q1.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Dine-in transaction volume grew about 56% consolidated (Barbeque India 60.8%), same-store sales grew 24.5%, and every market grew in double digits, though realisation fell 7-8% YoY with no price hike in four quarters.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management plans to add 40-50 restaurants annually from internal accruals with a raised FY30 target of 425-450, implying continued capex beyond the current 19 under construction.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Corporate cost at 10.3% of revenue, employee cost inflation of 6-7% at back-end and gross margin still flat YoY against a 100-150 bps improvement guide make a margin shortfall plausible.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Thailand entry (high setup costs) and the rightsized 3,000 sq ft store format are in rollout, and Big Buffet already runs in about 25% of restaurants, but no specific new product launch date was given.

rows.label: Selective price increases once volumes stabilise
rows.why: No price hike in four quarters and realisation down about 7-8% YoY; management cited selective future price increases but gave no timing or size.

rows.label: Premium CDR Mumbai/Delhi recovery
rows.why: Premium CDR SSSG was only 7.8% (base 5.5%) with new openings paused in Mumbai and Delhi for two quarters, while South India mature margins are above 18%.

rows.label: Net debt drifting up with expansion
rows.why: Net debt was marginally higher in Q2 as capex was largely offset by operating cash flow, and 40-50 openings a year are funded from internal accruals.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand breadth (SSSG above 20% in all four regions) and unit economics, but cautious on margin timing, declined a FY27 margin number and October two-year SSSG, and gave no next-year SSSG guide; analysts pushed on gross margin flat against guidance, corporate cost at 10.3%
